outcome: Teams can afford to keep log sources they used to drop, and search years of history fast enough to use mid-investigation.
overview: Retail security teams usually stop collecting logs long before they stop needing them, because the licensing model punishes volume. Falcon LogScale prices differently and searches without a conventional index, which changes what a team can afford to keep and how quickly it can ask a question of a year of data. The saving is real and specific: it applies to log platform cost, not to the security programme, and it should be compared against the incumbent’s actual renewal rather than its list price.

benefits.text: Log retention can be extended because cost does not scale the way an indexed platform’s does
benefits.limits: The comparison must be against the incumbent’s actual renewal, not list price; a heavily discounted incumbent narrows the gap considerably

benefits.text: Search over long time ranges is fast enough to be used during an investigation
benefits.limits: Search performance depends on query construction as much as on the platform; teams accustomed to an indexed platform need to relearn patterns

benefits.text: Sources previously dropped for cost can be onboarded
benefits.limits: The platform is agent-and-cloud, so telemetry leaves the customer estate; the tenant region is a design decision to be made and recorded rather than a default to be accepted

residency: Log data is held in the vendor platform in a selected region, recorded at design

notFor.situation: A team with a heavily discounted incumbent log platform and tuned content
notFor.why: The cost gap narrows and the content migration cost is real

notFor.situation: An estate with few log sources and no retention pressure
notFor.why: The economics that make this compelling do not apply at low volume

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited CrowdStrike implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks including a parallel run against the incumbent
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed content development.
1) Assessment — source inventory including dropped sources, measured volumes, incumbent renewal figure
2) Design — ingest plan, retention, content migration tranches and parallel-run criteria
3) Build — platform onboarded with the agreed sources, content migrated tranche by tranche
4) Parallel run and hand over — coverage compared against the incumbent, operations handed over
deliverables: Detection coverage during parallel run is at least equal to the incumbent’s for the migrated content
A search across the full retention period returns within the agreed time
Cost is reported against the incumbent renewal at equivalent source coverage
effort: 8–12 weeks including a parallel run against the incumbent
